Our research sits at the intersection of synchrotron science, artificial intelligence, and materials engineering. We develop the computational tools and experimental methods needed to make autonomous X-ray characterisation a reality.

---

## Self-Driving Microscopes

The core challenge: stochastic failure events in batteries (dendrite initiation, crack propagation, short-circuiting) are rare, fast, and invisible to pre-programmed experiments. We are building autonomous platforms where an AI pilot uses physics-based digital twins to steer beamlines in real-time, predicting and capturing these events as they happen.

This requires solving several coupled problems: training Graph Neural Networks to distinguish benign aging from true failure precursors, building simulation engines fast enough for real-time inference, and designing the control architecture that connects prediction to instrument action. We defined the operational requirements for this in the [BASE Scale](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2601.06978), a taxonomy for autonomous experimentation at large-scale facilities.

**Key papers:** [BASE Scale (arXiv, 2026)](/publication/2025-12-29-base-scale-autonomous-facilities/) · [Heuristic Operando Experimentation (arXiv, 2025)](/publication/2025-12-29-autonomous-battery-operando/)

## Operando Battery Characterisation

We design and run multi-modal operando experiments at UK national facilities (Diamond Light Source, ISIS, Central Laser Facility) to study how batteries degrade under realistic conditions. Our methods combine X-ray computed tomography with diffraction, fluorescence, and scattering to capture both structure and chemistry simultaneously.

As Principal Investigator, Le Houx leads the UK's Battery Imaging BAG at Diamond Light Source and has run 9 flagship experiments across Diamond, ISIS, and the Sirius synchrotron in Brazil.

**Key papers:** [Operando XCT of All-Solid-State Batteries](/publication/2025-08-14-operando-xct-assb/) · [Coupled X-ray Imaging/Diffraction in Soil Mechanics](/publication/2025-07-03-xray-soil-mechanics/)

## Computational Imaging and Machine Learning

We develop open-source computational tools to extract more information from 3D imaging data than conventional analysis allows:

- **Super-resolution**: Generative adversarial networks (EXG-GAN / [OpenLSR-X](https://github.com/jameslehoux)) that decouple the resolution/field-of-view trade-off in X-ray tomography, enabling high-resolution imaging at reduced dose and acquisition time.
- **Data fusion**: Methods to combine multi-modal, multi-resolution datasets (XCT + XRD-CT) into unified 3D maps of structure and chemistry.
- **Image-based simulation**: [OpenImpala](https://github.com/kramergroup/openImpala), our open-source C++ solver for computing effective transport properties directly from tomographic images, achieving 100x speedups over commercial solvers.
- **Data-driven mechanics**: D2IM-Strain, a deep learning framework (with Tozzi group, Greenwich) that predicts strain fields directly from undeformed XCT images, bypassing numerical differentiation and its associated noise.
- **Generative microstructures**: Physics-constrained diffusion models and GANs for generating synthetic 3D electrode microstructures that are statistically indistinguishable from real tomographic data.

**Key papers:** [Multimodal Synchrotron Data for ML (Scientific Data, 2025)](/publication/2025-02-24-multimodal-synchrotron-ml/) · [D2IM-Strain (bioRxiv, 2026)](/publication/2026-03-31-d2im-strain-bone/) · [OpenImpala (SoftwareX, 2021)](/publication/2021-07-01-openimpala-solver/)

## Quantum-AI for Scientific Imaging

An emerging research direction exploring whether quantum computing can address the computational bottlenecks in high-dimensional imaging. We are investigating quantum-native representations of volumetric image data and hybrid quantum-classical architectures for tasks such as segmentation, classification, and image correlation. This includes the conceptual development of Quantum Image Correlation (QuIC) as a future extension of digital volume correlation.
